name: GarageStack
description: GarageStack is an open-source vehicle monitoring dashboard for MG / SAIC electric, plug-in hybrid, and hybrid vehicles. It connects to the MG iSmart cloud via the SAIC MQTT Gateway and stores all data locally in an embedded PostgreSQL database. Features include: live dashboard, energy and efficiency statistics, trip history with heatmap visualisation, EV charging station overlay (requires free OCM API key), fuel station and motorway service area overlays (OpenStreetMap, no key required), Web Push notifications, and a Homepage dashboard widget. Everything runs in a single container -- no external database or MQTT broker required.

paths.name: Data Directory
paths.description: Persistent storage for the PostgreSQL database, MQTT data, application logs, and ASP.NET Data Protection keys. Back this up regularly.

ports.name: Web UI Port
ports.description: Host port for the GarageStack web interface. Open this in your browser.

ports.name: MQTT Port
ports.description: Host port for the internal Mosquitto MQTT broker. Leave blank (default) to keep the broker LAN-private. Only set if you need direct MQTT access from other devices, such as Home Assistant (see documentation/HOME_ASSISTANT.md).

variables.name: MG iSmart Email
variables.description: Your MG iSmart account email address. Must be the vehicle OWNER account -- shared or secondary accounts lack the write permissions needed to register alarm switches and will result in API error 1100003. Use a separate account on the MG phone app to avoid session conflicts.

variables.name: MG iSmart Password
variables.description: Your MG iSmart account password.

variables.name: MG Region
variables.description: Region your vehicle is registered in: eu (Europe, default), au (Australia/New Zealand), or tr (Turkiye). Automatically mapped to the right API endpoint.

variables.name: Database Password
variables.description: Password for the embedded PostgreSQL database. If left empty a strong random password is auto-generated on first start and saved to /data/.postgres_password inside the data directory. Set explicitly only if you need to connect to the database directly with external tools. Generate with: openssl rand -base64 24

variables.name: App URL
variables.description: The exact URL you use to open GarageStack in your browser, e.g. http://192.168.1.100:8080. Must match exactly -- wrong value causes login to fail.

variables.name: OIDC Issuer URL
variables.description: Optional. Issuer URL of your identity provider (Authentik, Authelia, Keycloak, Pocket ID, ...) -- the URL its /.well-known/openid-configuration sits under. Setting this switches GarageStack to single sign-on and disables the built-in password login. Register the redirect URI App URL/api/auth/oidc/callback at your provider. See documentation/AUTHENTICATION.md.

variables.name: OIDC Client ID
variables.description: Client ID issued by your identity provider for GarageStack. Required when OIDC Issuer URL is set.

variables.name: OIDC Client Secret
variables.description: Client secret issued by your identity provider. Leave empty for a public client that uses PKCE only.

variables.name: OIDC Allowed Groups
variables.description: Comma-separated groups allowed to sign in, e.g. garagestack-users. Leave empty only if your provider already restricts who can use this application -- otherwise every account it accepts can sign in and control your car.

variables.name: OIDC Allowed Emails
variables.description: Comma-separated email addresses allowed to sign in. Useful with providers that have no groups. Works alongside OIDC Allowed Groups -- a match on either list grants access.

variables.name: OIDC Provider Name
variables.description: Name shown on the sign-in button, e.g. Authentik.

variables.name: Keep Password Login With OIDC
variables.description: Set to true to keep the built-in username/password login available alongside single sign-on, e.g. as break-glass access for when your identity provider is down. Leave empty to switch it off automatically once OIDC is configured. Set AUTH_USERNAME and AUTH_PASSWORD to a strong dedicated password if you enable this.

variables.name: Login Username
variables.description: Username for the built-in web login. Leave empty to sign in with the MG iSmart email above.

variables.name: Login Password
variables.description: Password for the built-in web login. Leave empty to sign in with the MG iSmart password above. Set a strong dedicated password when the login stays enabled alongside single sign-on.

variables.name: Secure Session Cookie
variables.description: Set to true when GarageStack is served over HTTPS (behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy) so the session cookie is never sent over plain HTTP. Leave false for a plain-HTTP LAN install, or you will not be able to log in.

variables.name: Session Lifetime (hours)
variables.description: How long a single sign-on session lasts before the identity provider is consulted again. Signing in again is usually invisible while the provider's own session is still valid.

variables.name: OIDC Auto Login
variables.description: Set to true to skip the GarageStack login page and go straight to your identity provider.

variables.name: OIDC Scopes
variables.description: Scopes requested from the identity provider. Add the scope that carries group membership if your provider needs one for OIDC Allowed Groups.

variables.name: OIDC Groups Claim
variables.description: Name of the token claim that OIDC Allowed Groups is matched against. Provider-specific; groups covers most.

variables.name: OIDC Redirect URI
variables.description: Only needed when GarageStack cannot work out its own public URL, e.g. behind several chained reverse proxies. Must be App URL/api/auth/oidc/callback. Leave empty otherwise.

variables.name: OIDC Require HTTPS Metadata
variables.description: Set to false only for an identity provider served over plain HTTP on your LAN.

variables.name: Home Assistant MQTT Username
variables.description: Optional. Creates a broker login for the Home Assistant MQTT integration, limited to the car's topics. The car then appears in Home Assistant automatically. Also set the MQTT Port above so Home Assistant can reach the broker. See documentation/HOME_ASSISTANT.md.

variables.name: Home Assistant MQTT Password
variables.description: Password for the Home Assistant MQTT login. Required when Home Assistant MQTT Username is set. Generate with: openssl rand -hex 32

variables.name: Internal MQTT Username
variables.description: Login the SAIC gateway, API and Worker use on the bundled Mosquitto broker. Only relevant if you connect other MQTT clients to the exposed MQTT port.

variables.name: Internal MQTT Password
variables.description: Password for the internal broker login. Leave empty to have a random one generated at every start (fine unless external MQTT clients need a stable password). Generate with: openssl rand -hex 32

variables.name: MG API Endpoint Override
variables.description: Optional. Only needed if your region isn't eu, au, or tr -- set directly to your gateway's endpoint.

variables.name: VAPID Public Key
variables.description: VAPID public key for Web Push notifications. Leave empty to disable push notifications (the rest of the app works fine without them). Generate a key pair with: npx web-push generate-vapid-keys

variables.name: VAPID Private Key
variables.description: VAPID private key for Web Push notifications. Keep this secret.

variables.name: Notification Language
variables.description: Language of the push notification texts (Engine started, Door left open, ...): en or nl. Notifications are written by the background worker, which has no browser to take a language from, so this is set per deployment.

variables.name: Homepage Widget API Key
variables.description: Static API key for the read-only /api/widget/{vin}/status endpoint used by the gethomepage.dev Custom API widget. Leave empty to keep the endpoint disabled. Generate with: openssl rand -base64 32

variables.name: Open Charge Map API Key
variables.description: API key for the EV charging station overlay on the map. Free to obtain at https://openchargemap.org/site/develop -- create an account and generate a key. Leave empty to disable the charging station feature.

variables.name: Overpass API Base URL
variables.description: Overpass API endpoint used for fuel station and motorway service area overlays. Defaults to the public endpoint -- no API key required. Change this only if you self-host an Overpass instance.

variables.name: Speed Camera Layer Enabled
variables.description: Offers a map layer of the speed cameras mapped in OpenStreetMap. No API key required, and the layer stays off until you switch it on in the map's layer panel. Set to false to remove it from the deployment entirely -- do that where showing a driver where the cameras are is restricted, France and Germany among others.

variables.name: Reverse Geocoding Enabled
variables.description: Turns coordinates into place names via OpenStreetMap Nominatim: city names in the trip list and the street the car is parked in. No API key required, and answers are cached for 90 days. Set to false to keep coordinates off a third-party service -- the trip list then shows dates.

variables.name: Nominatim Base URL
variables.description: Nominatim endpoint used for those place names. Defaults to the public instance -- no API key required. Change this only if you self-host Nominatim.

variables.name: Map Matching Enabled
variables.description: Draws a selected trip along the roads it was driven on, snapped onto OpenStreetMap by Valhalla, instead of in straight lines between GPS fixes. No API key required, and snapped trips are cached for 30 days. Set to false to keep trip geometry off a third-party service -- trips are then drawn from their raw fixes.

variables.name: Valhalla Base URL
variables.description: Valhalla endpoint used for that snapping. Defaults to the public instance -- no API key required. Change this only if you self-host Valhalla.

variables.name: Tyre Pressure - Low (bar)
variables.description: Tyre pressure (bar) below which a tyre is shown red / triggers a low-pressure alert. Override to match your vehicle's placarded pressure.

variables.name: Tyre Pressure - Good (bar)
variables.description: Tyre pressure (bar) at and above which a tyre is shown green (healthy). Below this and above the low threshold, it is shown orange.

variables.name: Tyre Pressure - High (bar)
variables.description: Tyre pressure (bar) above which a tyre is shown red / triggers an over-inflation alert.

variables.name: HV Battery Capacity (kWh)
variables.description: Usable capacity of the traction battery, in kWh. The MQTT gateway assumes an EV-sized pack rather than reading the real one, so the kWh it reports are far too large on a plain hybrid (an MG HS Hybrid+ carries 1.83 kWh and is reported as 72.5). Leave empty to keep the gateway's figure on a BEV or PHEV and show charge as a percentage only on a hybrid.

variables.name: Database Name
variables.description: PostgreSQL database name. Only change this if you know what you are doing.

variables.name: Database User
variables.description: PostgreSQL database user. Only change this if you know what you are doing.
